### PiliBabel

AI interface & content translation layered on top of **PiliNara / PiliPlus** — the whole app speaks your language.

**Install**
*Android* — download `PiliBabel.apk` below, allow “install unknown apps”, and open it. Every release is signed with the **stable PiliBabel key**, so newer versions **upgrade in place** (no uninstall needed) and the app keeps coexisting with PiliNara.
*Desktop* — `PiliBabel_windows_*` (portable zip / setup exe) and `PiliBabel_linux_*` (deb / rpm / AppImage / tar.gz) are attached to each release.

**What's new**
- **A Chinese target language no longer spends your API tokens on comments.** With the target set to Chinese, PiliBabel now behaves exactly like PiliNara / PiliPlus: nothing is auto-translated through your own endpoint. Foreign comments are covered by bilibili's own **free** translation — the per-comment 「翻译」 button (gRPC `ReplyItem/TranslateReply`), which has always been in the app. Where the original translates nothing, we translate nothing either, so the danmaku-translate button is now **hidden** for Chinese targets rather than silently doing nothing. Any non-Chinese target keeps the previous behaviour: your configured API does the translating. The settings copy next to the language picker says which mode you are in.
- **The player's 画面比例 (aspect-ratio) menu is translated now.** 拉伸 / 自动 / 裁剪 / 等宽 / 等高 / 原始 / 限制 / 4:3 / 16:9 were hard-coded enum labels — in both the player and the live-room control bars. They now go through the translation pipeline, are pre-warmed as soon as the player UI renders (a popup menu is built once, so waiting until it opens is too late), and live-update if the translation arrives after it is already open.
- **Turning AI translation off now restores *all* original text.** Three places had cached the translated strings and could never go back: the settings list's per-option subtitles (a `static final` list, so `uiTx()` was evaluated once at class initialisation), every settings sub-page's item list (captured in `initState`), and the settings search index (`late final`). All three now resolve the source text at render time inside a reactive builder, so switching translation off reverts them immediately.
- **The danmaku-translation confirmation dialog is fixed and now animates in.** Three things:
  * its warning line is now sourced in **English** — `Danmaku AI translation consumes a lot of tokens. Continue?` — so it stays readable when interface translation is off, not configured yet, or still in flight;
  * it is now **actually translated into your target language**. A dialog is built exactly once, so without a reactive dependency a translation that arrives *after* the dialog opened could never appear — the source line stayed frozen on screen even with the target language set to Japanese. The dialog body is now wrapped in a reactive builder, so the translation replaces the text in place as soon as it lands (and it is still pre-warmed while the player controls render, so it is usually already translated before you tap);
  * all three references to that line now share one constant, so the pre-warm key can never drift from the rendered key — a silent mismatch there would make pre-warming useless.
  * it also **fades in with a slight rise and scale over 220 ms** (via `showGeneralDialog`) instead of snapping into view.
- **Optional: adapt the bitrate to your actual speed** — *Me → Settings → Player → 带宽不足时自动降低画质*, **off by default**; you decide whether the app may change your quality. When you turn it on: the "plays 1–2 s, stalls 3–4 s, repeats" cycle has exactly one root cause — sustained throughput below the stream's bitrate — and no buffer size can fix it (a bigger buffer only postpones the stall). The player measures *content seconds advanced ÷ seconds elapsed* over 15-second windows and, after two consecutive windows below 60 %, drops to **the highest quality tier your measured speed can actually carry** — in one step, not one tier at a time (walking 8K → 1080P one tier per round would take minutes of stuttering), and resumes from the same position.
- **Automatic line-switching stays a separate, off-by-default switch** (*Me → Settings → Player → 卡顿时自动换线（实验）*). The quality drop never switches edges, so it cannot land on a rejected candidate — the failure mode behind the earlier "video track died while audio kept playing, then reload gave a black screen". Both switches now live on the Player settings page, and their labels/descriptions go through the AI-translation pipeline like the rest of the UI.
- **A measuring bug that made the old self-healing a no-op.** mpv's `cache-pause` sets `pause=yes` whenever the cache runs dry, and `media_kit` derives `stream.playing` straight from `pause` — so during the very stalls the watchdog exists to catch, `isPlaying` was `false` and the guard reset the measurement window on every hiccup. A 15-second window could therefore never complete, and the throughput ratio was never computed: the "slow line" self-healing added back in v0.2.12 had never once fired. The guard now only treats a *user* pause / EOF / backgrounding as "don't measure" (using mpv's `paused-for-cache` signal), so windows accumulate across stalls. The app also starts at the **highest tier your account can access** (upstream default, up to 8K/HDR) — worth knowing when comparing against the official app, which starts at 1080P.
- **Video & audio stream URLs now come from the same source as the official bilibili app.** Playback no longer uses the web endpoint `/x/player/wbi/playurl` — it uses the app's own gRPC `bilibili.app.playurl.v1.PlayURL/PlayView`, and the media request is fingerprinted the way the app fingerprints it. This is not cosmetic: the CDN validates the request against the *token's* issuing client. Measured on the same video from the same IP — a **web** token is only accepted together with `Referer: https://www.bilibili.com` **and**, on `upos-*-mirror*ov` edges, a Safari/macOS user-agent (Chrome and BiliDroid UAs get a hard `403`); an **app** token is only accepted with **no** `Referer` at all (any UA). The two are mutually exclusive, so the old web path was one UA/header change away from losing the video track — and the audio page, which already used the app endpoint, is exactly why it never stuttered while video did. Streams are now played in the order bilibili hands them out (no edge-picking, no host rewriting), and the player switches `user-agent`/`referrer` per source. The web call is still issued **in parallel**, purely for the metadata the app endpoint doesn't return (subtitle-language list, resume position, clip info), so nothing else regresses. Switch: *Settings → Player → 直链取流与官方 APP 一致* — on by default, off restores the old web behaviour.
- AI interface & content translation with **translate-once + local persistence** — never re-translated on reopen.
- ~35 target languages via **your own** OpenAI-compatible endpoint; the translation endpoint is fully **independent** from AI video summary.
- Per-comment **Original ⇄ Translation** toggle; hyperlinks are preserved and stay clickable.
- **Danmaku translation** — an independent player toggle that pre-translates ahead of the playhead in ~15-second batches.
- **Thinking-mode** switch, **test-translate**, and a batched/concurrent pipeline (progressive per-chunk apply for faster first load).
- **Tap-to-switch caching, always responsive.** Tapping any queued item starts it **immediately** and sends the item that was downloading back to the queue — there is no download lock any more, so a stalled edge or a hung metadata request can never make the list ignore your taps. A hard failure now names its reason, and the queue moves on to the next item instead of dying on the first one.
- **First-launch onboarding** dialog pointing to *Settings → AI → AI interface translation*, with a one-tap shortcut to that page.
- **Toggle semantics are now explicit**: turning AI translation **off** falls back to the original text everywhere and issues **zero** API requests (your token/quota is never touched); turning it **on** translates foreign-language content — e.g. comments — into your selected language.
- **Worldwide playback**: outside mainland China the player now picks bilibili's own **overseas edges** (Akamai / `mirror*ov`) straight from the geo-routed stream URLs instead of forcing a China-only mirror, which is what caused “audio plays, video freezes” and endless retry toasts.
- **Mid-playback video stalls, done properly this time.** DASH video and audio are two separate signed URLs, so a throttled edge can starve only the video: mpv reports **no error at all**, and its position keeps advancing on the **audio** clock — which is exactly why the previous “position frozen” watchdog could never fire and v0.2.10 felt unchanged. Detection now uses the buffer itself (`buffering` sustained / forward buffer drained) held for **20 seconds**, and recovery is tiered and rate-limited: switch to another edge bilibili already handed us (never a rewritten host, so no 403), else re-request the playurl — at most once every **3 minutes**, at most **3 times per 10 minutes**, and short 2–5 s hiccups are left to the buffer instead of being “fixed” by a reopen that throws the buffer away.
- **The automatic line-switching / quality-dropping is now opt-in and OFF by default** (*Settings → Player → 卡顿时自动换线/降画质（实验）*) while the failure mode behind it is investigated. Reported sequence: stutters started, then the **video track died while audio kept playing**, then “重载视频” gave a black screen. The mechanism that fits best: an automatic switch can land on a candidate whose **video** URL is rejected (403 from an overseas IP) while its audio URL still delivers — mpv then plays audio over a frozen picture and emits **no error at all**, so nothing recovers, and a reload re-requests into the same situation. A user-configured custom CDN node rewrites hosts the same way and has exactly the same failure mode. With the switch off the player issues **no** automatic re-opens at all (upstream behaviour). Also: picture parameters are re-applied after a manual line switch.
- **Single-loop no longer parks at the end (video as well as audio).** The video player's “从头播放” path had the same defect as the audio page: it seeked to 0 *before* `play()`, and `seek()` clears `media_kit`'s `completed` flag — which is exactly the flag `play()` needs in order to perform the real restart — so it degraded into a no-op `pause=false` and could freeze on the last frame with the play button still showing *playing* (its inner seek wasn't even awaited, so it also raced). It now plays first, verifies 250 ms later, and only then falls back to an explicit `pause → seek(0) → play`.
- **Audio single-loop no longer stops at 00:00.** On the audio page, “单个循环” could finish, snap the bar back to 00:00 and then just sit there with the play button still showing *playing* — occasionally, but often. Cause: `media_kit`'s `play()` only performs the real restart (seek to 0 → `playlist-pos=0` → unpause) **while `state.completed` is still true**, and the old fallback called `seek(0)` *first* — which clears `completed` — so `play()` degenerated into a no-op `pause=false` on a player that was already parked at EOF, while still emitting "playing" to the UI. The restart now calls `play()` **first**, while `completed` is still set, so the library performs its full restart; it verifies 250 ms later and only then falls back to an explicit `pause() → seek(0) → play()` (which is also what makes a manual tap on the play button recover from a stuck state). Also fixed: the `completed:false` event emitted after a seek was being reported to the media session as “playback finished”.
- **A line that is merely *slow* now heals itself too.** The previous watchdog only saw a *frozen* player, so the classic overseas pattern — play 1–2 s, stall 5 s, repeat forever — never triggered it (every 2 s of playback reset the counter) and no buffer size can fix it, because the line's throughput is simply below the stream's bitrate. The player now measures **content seconds advanced ÷ seconds elapsed** over 15-second windows; two consecutive bad windows (under 60 %) mean *this line can't carry this bitrate*, and it escalates: switch to another edge bilibili already handed us → if that still can't keep up, **automatically drop one quality tier** (toast: 已自动降低画质, position preserved) → and if there is no other edge and you are already at the lowest tier, it re-requests the playurl once and then **stops touching anything** instead of looping.
- **Bigger default video buffer (4 MB → 32 MB forward).** 4 MB is only ~4 s of an 8 Mbps stream and ~1–2 s of 4K, so any overseas throttle drained it and produced the “stutters every few seconds” cycle. The default demuxer buffer is now 32 MB (~16 s, still clamped by 缓冲时长), addressable in *Settings → Player → 缓冲大小*. Live streams keep their own small cap so the picture never drifts far behind the live edge.
- **Downloads**: a stalled line is now decided in **5 seconds of zero bytes** — switch to the next signed edge, at most twice (so one task tries 3 lines); when there is nothing left to switch to, it either **yields** to another queued item (partial file kept, fresh stream URLs when its turn comes again) or, if nothing else is queued, reports **download failed**. On top of that, a matching 5s “no new bytes in **any** phase” **global** watchdog also covers the phases where the per-line timer isn't running yet (a switched edge that accepts the connection but never replies) — that was the old “frozen at a fixed MB forever” bug. Rotation keeps resuming from the partial file, audio no longer gets corrupted by rejected Range requests, a line trickling below ~32 KB/s on the last edge re-requests fresh stream URLs (or fails), danmaku fetching is time-boxed and optional so a slow overseas `dm` endpoint can't wedge the queue, and if the queue is ever held up longer than 8s the UI names the stage it is stuck in. Any hard failure now surfaces with its reason (disk write errors and other non-HTTP exceptions can no longer leave a row sitting on “downloading” forever), and when an item fails for good the queue automatically moves on to the next one instead of dying on the first failure.
- **Downloads**: a stalled line is now decided in **5 seconds of zero bytes** — switch to the next signed edge, at most twice (so one task tries 3 lines); when there is nothing left to switch to, it either **yields** to another queued item (partial file kept, fresh stream URLs when its turn comes again) or, if nothing else is queued, reports **download failed**. On top of that, a matching 5s “no new bytes in **any** phase” **global** watchdog also covers the phases where the per-line timer isn't running yet (a switched edge that accepts the connection but never replies) — that was the old “frozen at a fixed MB forever” bug. - **Faster caching from overseas.** The downloader now keeps an **Akamai global-edge variant** of each signed stream URL as an extra candidate, and treats anything under **512 KB/s** as slow enough to switch (the old bar was 64 KB/s, so a mainland edge throttled to ~100 KB/s was never abandoned — that was the “always 100 KB/s in Japan” report).
- **Audio progress is shown too.** During “downloading audio” the row now reports combined video+audio MB / MB instead of a blank, so long exports no longer look frozen at the last video byte.

**Fork lineage**: PiliBabel → PiliNara → PiliPlus → PiliPala. GPL-3.0, same as upstream.
